# scylladbcloud_cluster_backup_retention (Resource)

Manages how long the backups of a deleted cluster are kept. A cluster has a backup retention only after it is deleted with `backup_retention_days` above 0; destroying this resource leaves the retention as it is.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Keep the backups of a deleted cluster for 14 days. The cluster must have
# been deleted with backup_retention_days above 0.
resource "scylladbcloud_cluster_backup_retention" "example" {
	cluster_id     = 1337
	retention_days = 14
}

output "scylladbcloud_backup_retention_start_date" {
	value = scylladbcloud_cluster_backup_retention.example.start_date
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (Number) ID of the deleted cluster whose backups are kept.
- `retention_days` (Number) Days to keep the backups, counted from `start_date`, between 0 and 60. 0 cancels the retention and the backups are deleted at the next check.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `encryption_keys` (List of String) IDs of the encryption keys kept for the backups.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `start_date` (String) When the retention started (RFC 3339).

### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

- `create` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by the ID of the deleted cluster.
terraform import scylladbcloud_cluster_backup_retention.example 1337
```
